Subject: Geofence acceptance criteria and scrub evidence request

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for taking this. We are finalizing the technical acceptance for our Dedicated deployment and need a clear checklist and sample artifacts to present to our internal auditors. Specifically they want the following confirmed and demonstrated:

- How tenant geofencing (site-anchoring) is enforced end-to-end (control plane vs compute plane).
- Concrete evidence for a tenant-level wipe (what logs/artifacts we can expect to receive).
- Handling of snapshots and cross-region replication (are snapshots pinned, are there retained copies elsewhere?).
- Typical timeline from request to certificate of completion for a deletion.

Could you send a short acceptance checklist, example scrub log, and any diagrams showing snapshot lifecycle and what we can expect in evidence handoff? We need to review with compliance by EOD Friday (22 Aug).

Thanks,
Alex

FinTrust

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>

Date: Sun, 17 Aug 2025 13:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Geofence acceptance criteria and scrub evidence request

Alex — thanks, we can absolutely provide that. High level answers and the artifacts we will attach:

- Enforcement:
  - Control plane records the tenant pin and placement policy; serving runtime schedules pods to pinned hosts and a routing layer enforces region affinity. Network ACLs and hypervisor placement rules prevent cross-region replicas for pinned tenants.

- Wipe evidence:
  - You will receive a signed artifact bundle that includes: a scrub log (CSV of deleted object ids + timestamps), associated snapshot manifests (SHA256 checksums), and an operations attestation signed by our on-call engineer.

- Snapshots/replication:
  - By default, snapshots for pinned tenants are stored only in the pinned region. Automated backups are subject to the tenancy policy: we can enable retention hold windows (e.g., 0/7/30 days). We will flag and exclude cross-region replication for your dedicated cluster.

- Timeline:
  - Standard erase request -> ops scheduling: 24–48 hours (business)
  - Execution + verification: 1–3 business days depending on dataset size
  - Attestation bundle delivery: within 24 hours after verification

Action items I will attach in this thread:
- redwood_residency_acceptance_checklist.pdf (detailed acceptance steps + pass/fail examples)
- sample_wipe_log_20250430.csv (synthetic scrub log showing object ids, timestamps, operator id)
- snapshot-pruning-diagram.png (lifecycle diagram)

Marissa & Ben — looping you in for commercial acceptance and a quick technical confirmation on the snapshot guarantees.

Regards,
Rachel Kim
Account Lead, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Rachel / Alex — quick technical clarifications from ops:

1) Snapshots: our pruning job is incremental and snapshot manifests include a list of block ids and checksums. When a deletion request runs we mark relevant blocks as tombstoned and run a sweep that ensures no live pointers remain. The artifact will include the pre- and post- snapshot manifests (so you can verify checksums).

2) Backups: we will disable any cross-region backup policies for the dedicated pool for FinTrust. If you later request cross-region replication we will require explicit change approval and provide a new attestation.

3) Retention holds / legal holds: we can set a temporary retention hold for a rolling window (e.g., 30 days) if you need a buffer for legal review; the acceptance checklist includes fail/pass criteria for holds.

I attached the sample scrub log and snapshot diagram for Alex to review.
